Topic 14.2: Water orientation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Water orientation. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Demonstrate ability to take care 15 lessons safety precautions when playing with water for personal safety
2. Demonstrate basic swimming skills for talent development
3. Have fun when playing with in in water baby pool basic swimming styles in turns

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Demonstrate ability to take care 15 lessons safety precautions when playing with water for personal safety
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to demonstrate ability to take care 15 lessons safety precautions when playing with water for personal safety. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. Demonstrate basic swimming skills for talent development
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to demonstrate basic swimming skills for talent development. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. Have fun when playing with in in water baby pool basic swimming styles in turns
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to have fun when playing with in in water baby pool basic swimming styles in turns. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At home, obey your parent when they ask you to wash your plate. That shows obedience.

Example 2: Tell the truth if you break a cup. Saying what really happened is honesty.

Example 3: Thank God for your family before you sleep. A short prayer can be: “Thank you God for today.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Water orientation.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Water orientation. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Water orientation important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
